communityDay.name: Community Day Services
communityDay.tagline: Building Skills. Exploring Interests. Connecting with Others.

blocks.text: Community Day Services (CDS) offers a variety of classes, experiences and vocational opportunities that help each man build on his strengths, maintain skills and explore his interests. Learning reflects each participant’s individual goals, supporting confidence and greater independence in everyday life.

Through social activities, personal living skills, physical fitness, technology and vocational training, participants have opportunities to learn, connect and grow. Browse our classes below to see how we bring learning to life.

blocks.caption: Learning and connecting through hands-on activities in Community Day Services.

blocks.text: From recognizing money to planning purchases, Economics connects basic math skills with everyday decisions. Participants practice identifying and writing numbers, understanding money values, using calculators and learning about banking. Budgeting for shopping trips and outings helps each man put these skills into practice while managing his personal funds.

The Personal Living Skills curriculum combines applied skill development tailored to empower men on their journey to self-sufficiency. These skills include personal hygiene, including hand hygiene, shaving, nail care, hair grooming, oral hygiene routines, laundry, bed-making and kitchen cooking, baking and cleaning.

Experiments like the ‘Glitter Bug’ illuminate the importance of thorough handwashing, revealing the lingering remnants of glitter (germs) left behind. Plaque disclosing tablets or sprays unveil the hidden realms needing extra care during oral hygiene rituals. Moreover, a mock bedroom sanctuary serves as a practical haven for perfecting bed-making finesse and the art of laundry organization, ensuring that learning transcends the mundane to become a vibrant, hands-on adventure.

Another component of Personal Living Skills is environmental interaction, a very broad area that includes using safety skills, using different types of transportation and using community facilities, such as the library.

At Good Shepherd Manor, technology is more than a modern amenity — it’s a gateway to opportunity. It opens doors to independence, education, communication, and meaningful personal growth. For our clients, access to technology means access to the wider world, on their own terms.

Our former computer lab, equipped with just a few aging machines, struggled to meet that need. Wait times were long, technical issues frequent, and the setup did not accommodate varying sensory or cognitive needs. The limitations were frustrating not only for our residents, but also for the staff supporting them. We knew it was time for a change.
Funded in 2025, the former computer lab received a major upgrade and is now affectionately referred to as the Digital Den. The lab is designed to serve a broad range of users and learning styles.
The lab features:

items: Modern modular desks with privacy partitions, to reduce distractions and support focused use
A SMART Board interactive flat panel, for group learning, collaborative games, and classroom-style instruction
Amazon Fire HD tablets with noise-canceling headphones, allowing for flexible, accessible engagement with content
Upgraded wiring and secure cable management, with lockable furniture to protect devices and ensure long-term functionality

blocks.text: These upgrades aren’t just about better equipment, they’re about better experiences. Each addition is tailored to meet residents where they are and empower them to engage, learn, and grow.

Whether it’s watching favorite shows, learning how to type, sending messages to family, or simply enjoying music in a quiet moment, each use of the Digital Den represents personal progress and meaningful engagement.

While some may assume that individuals with IDD lack the capacity to engage with political matters, this perception is not only misleading but also overlooks the potential of many. Some individuals with intellectual disabilities can indeed understand complex political issues and engage meaningfully in the democratic and electoral process.
Conversations around current events are welcomed, allowing men who desire to do so to express their thoughts and opinions.

This class uses education and skill building to address all aspects of physical activity, fitness and mobility. Through games and exercises the clients learn about the importance of weight control and remaining physically active.

In 2023, Assembly Hall in CDS was transformed into a recreational space. This space offers men the benefit of audio-visual equipment used to stream exercise videos specifically tailored to individuals with developmental disabilities and/or limited mobility. There are also a wide range of activities included in this class that promotes physical health, mental sharpness, and social interaction.

Activities such as Chair Yoga usually start the day. During this activity, men find solace and tranquility in gentle stretches and guided breathing exercises. This practice not only promotes flexibility but also promotes a sense of relaxation and mindfulness. Men find themselves embracing a moment of calm before diving into the day’s activities.

Games along the lines of Finish the Phrase, What Am I, and Hangman are often played after physical activities and spark lively anticipation as participants complete well-known phrases or proverbs, guess the object, or solve the word. Laughter fills the room as quick thinking, creative wordplay, and humorous guesses come to life. Such games serve as a mental workout, stimulating men’s mental agility and showcasing their wit.

A fan favorite is indoor baseball. With a soft beach ball and cushioned baseball bat in hand, men take to the makeshift field. Bases marked with chairs provide resting spots between runs, ensuring that everyone can participate. This activity fosters friendly competition, physical activity, and a true sense of community.

The Scavenger Hunt is another favorite among the men. The hunt injects a sense of adventure into the day. Armed with clues, men embark on a thrilling quest, exploring every nook and cranny of the rec room, sometimes spilling into other areas of the Community Day Center. This activity stimulates problem-solving skills, ignites creativity, and keeps bodies in motion.

The Indoor Parachute activity brings together teamwork and physical exertion. Men gather around a large parachute, working in synchrony to lift and lower it, creating vibrant waves of color that fill the room. This cooperative workout not only strengthens their arms but also fosters camaraderie and a sense of unity among participants.

These activities are just a few examples of the diverse range of physical and mindful activities offered. Every week, the recreation space introduces new and exciting ways to stay active and sharp. This dynamic approach ensures that Manor men always have something fresh and engaging to look forward to. With each passing week, they embrace new challenges, forge stronger connections, and continue to thrive in this vibrant recreational haven.

The vocational room allows residents to explore a variety of vocational skills, such as, sorting, folding, filing and stuffing. Skills are taught and maintained through pre-established exercises that can prepare the residents for employment or just building skills. There are opportunities for the men in the vocational classrooms to work in the GSM kitchen, the local food pantry, office work at GSM and Navarro Farms.
Serving Stars

A recent program called Serving Stars served as a great example of how the vocational classes were able to utilize the technology in the Digital Den. Serving Stars began with a simple idea: give residents with work and volunteer experience a chance to build on what they already knew. Due to the experience in the Vocational classroom the residents understood the basics of being ready for work. Serving Stars gave them a chance to explore why those expectations matter while using technology, sharing their experiences, and learning from one another.
Lessons in the Serving Stars program covered workplace readiness, hygiene, food safety, teamwork, restaurant operations, and communication.

There are two classrooms in a self-contained setting designed to address the needs of the clients who are showing signs of aging, are at retirement age or beyond, and have had to make some modifications in life due to aging. This area supports increased interaction but at a pace more conducive to the individual client’s circumstances.

The goal for these classrooms are to assist the residents to remain active and maintain existing skills, to provide opportunities to interact with others who have the same issues and challenges related to aging, to assist in developing coping skills and strategies in dealing with all aspects of aging and to foster an atmosphere of peer support. Both of these classrooms provide a comfortable environment that supports age related changes for each individual, both physically and mentally.

sections.title: Additional Activities in Community Day Services

blocks.text: Star-based reward system

Men now earn stars for active participation in each class, which they can redeem for snacks, games, or save up for the much-loved All-Star Lunch. Each month, the top four earners pick their restaurant and choose a staff member to accompany them. There has been a noticeable boost in motivation, pride, and camaraderie.
Birthday Celebrations

Every month, the men come together to celebrate those with birthdays, and it’s become a highlight of the CDS experience. The Personal Living Skills class helps bake treats for the celebration, learning and building practical kitchen skills along the way. It’s a chance to grow while giving back and the joy it brings is shared by everyone in the room.
Outings Calendar

In recent years the outing calendar has been transformed into a passport to new experiences. Men are venturing out to the Strickler Planetarium at Olivet Nazarene University to explore the stars. They’re spending time outdoors with animals at Sandy Oaks Ranch and relaxing with watercolor painting under the trees at Willow Haven Nature Preserve, opportunities that awaken creativity, confidence, and joy.

And then there’s Navarro Farm, a nonprofit farm designed for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. GSM men head there to learn real agricultural skills and contribute to something meaningful. But more than that, they’re growing a deep sense of independence, purpose, and pride, alongside others who believe in their ability to succeed.

A full life includes places to explore, people to meet, and experiences to look forward to. At Good Shepherd Manor, community engagement begins with each man’s interests. Whether he enjoys competing in sports, performing on stage, discovering nature, or sharing dinner with friends, we help him take part in activities that bring meaning and enjoyment to his life.

blocks.caption: Placeholder photo — outings, athletics, and community events.

blocks.text: The men enjoy a wide variety of outings throughout Momence, the surrounding communities of Kankakee County and the Chicagoland area. A weekend might include cheering at a sporting event, catching a movie, attending a concert, or watching a local theater production. Dining out and shopping offer opportunities to make choices, practice everyday skills, and spend time together.

Other adventures take the men even farther from Momence such as exploring Fair Oaks Farms, visiting zoos and enjoying yacht trips on Lake Michigan. Celebrations, festivals, and local happenings offer new experiences alongside familiar favorites. Each outing creates opportunities to connect with others and participate in community life.

sections.title: Teamwork, Confidence, and the Joy of Competition

blocks.text: More than 50 of our men compete in Special Olympics across more than 10 sports. Through practices and competitions athletes develop skills, build confidence, and form friendships with teammates and fellow competitors.

The experience extends beyond the competition itself. Working toward a personal goal, encouraging a teammate, and celebrating an accomplishment give the men opportunities to take pride in their efforts and share their enthusiasm with others.

For men who enjoy the arts, participation in GSM’s Chorus, or Easy Street Theater productions offer opportunities for creative expression, teamwork, and the excitement of performing for an audience. Attending other local productions, exploring art, and enjoying live music provide additional ways to enjoy personal interests.
Whether participating or applauding from the audience, the men are part of the creative life of their community.

Warmer months bring opportunities for picnics, park visits, farm outings, and outdoor events. Places such as Perry Farm, Island Park, the Kankakee River State Park, nature reserves and many other local parks offer settings for fresh air, time with friends, and the enjoyment of nature.

Some men look forward to an active excursion; others prefer a leisurely outing and a quiet place to take in their surroundings. A variety of experiences allows each man to enjoy the outdoors in ways that suit his interests and comfort.
Community engagement also means contributing. Volunteering gives the men opportunities to share their abilities, help others, and take pride in their role within the community by giving back.

Attending community Mass and joining local celebrations strengthen connections with neighbors and offer meaningful ways to express faith and share traditions. Through these everyday encounters, the men build relationships and become familiar, valued members of the places they visit.
Connections grow in both directions. Along with participating in life beyond our campus, the men are involved in GSM events that welcome neighbors, families, and friends to the Manor.
Fall Festival
Held on the second Saturday of September, this annual tradition brings the GSM family and wider community together for a day of activities and celebration.
Annual Touch A Truck
A free community event held the first weekend of October, offering opportunities for visitors of all ages and abilities to explore vehicles and meet the people who operate them.
Twelfth Night Bonfire
A January gathering that brings people together to share a seasonal tradition.
Free Outdoor Community Movies
Welcoming opportunities to enjoy a movie outdoors and spend time together at GSM.
These events offer more than a visit to our campus. They create opportunities to get to know the men, share experiences, and build lasting connections.

blocks.text: At Good Shepherd Manor, home means safety and belonging, dignity and compassion. It means familiar routines, meaningful relationships, and knowing someone will notice when you are struggling and celebrate when you succeed.
We are honored to create that sense of home for the men we serve and grateful for the trust their families place in us.

blocks.caption: Placeholder photo — homes on the Momence campus.

blocks.text: All thirteen of Good Shepherd Manor’s residential homes operate as Community Integrated Living Arrangements, or CILAs. This model emphasizes individualized support, personal choice, and community involvement while providing the assistance each man needs in daily life.

Each home offers a family-like atmosphere, with residents gathering for family-style breakfasts and dinners each day. With support suited to their abilities, the men help with cooking, cleaning, vacuuming, laundry, and other household responsibilities. These everyday activities build practical skills, encourage independence, and nurture pride in their shared home.

Dedicated staff provide support around the clock, helping each man build independence, maintain relationships, and participate in activities he enjoys. Each person’s needs, preferences, routines, and compatibility with housemates help guide a comfortable and welcoming home environment.

Shared meals, outings, celebrations, and opportunities for prayer bring people together. Whether enjoying a quiet evening with housemates or welcoming families for special events, these experiences strengthen the connections that make GSM home.

Quality care begins with listening and being present. Through Shepherd’s Rounds, named in tribute to the Brothers who first stewarded this community, members of our senior leadership team visit homes each week to connect with the men and staff.

These visits provide opportunities to hear concerns, recognize what is working well, and address challenges promptly. They strengthen relationships and keep leadership connected to everyday life in our homes.

The people who work in our homes are central to the quality of life the men experience. Staff training, including Safety Care, helps team members respond compassionately, de-escalate challenging situations, and support everyone’s safety.

Developing leaders from within our team brings firsthand knowledge of residential life into supervisory roles. Clear documentation and communication tools, including the GSM Portal, help staff share information and provide consistent support across homes.

A dependable environment helps the men feel comfortable and confident in their daily lives. Maintaining heating, cooling, power, and lighting is an essential part of that commitment. Preventive maintenance and thoughtful upgrades help reduce unexpected disruptions and preserve familiar routines.

Improvements to boilers and heating and cooling equipment support comfort throughout the seasons. Whole-home generators, made possible through the generosity of families and donors, help residents remain in their homes during power outages. Planning for maintenance and eventual replacement helps preserve that reliability.
Lighting along walkways, parking areas, and circle drives improves visibility after dark, supporting movement across campus and participation in activities.

An upgraded communication system, radios, and campus technology help residential staff coordinate with nursing, supervisors, and support services during daily activities and emergencies. Maintaining these systems helps staff share information and respond when needs arise.

sections.title: Growing with the Men We Serve

blocks.text: Since our founding in 1971, Good Shepherd Manor has adapted to meet the changing needs of the men entrusted to our care. The Brothers and founding families helped establish a community that recognized the abilities, dignity, and humanity of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

In the 1990s, GSM began moving away from dormitory-style living into Intermediate Care Facility homes and later opened smaller CILA homes. These changes supported greater privacy, personal choice, and opportunities for connection.

Making home happen is the everyday work of Good Shepherd Manor. It is found in trusted relationships, shared laughter, thoughtful support, and quiet moments of kindness—and in the attention that keeps each home running smoothly.

Dedicated staff, supportive families, generous donors, and community partners make this work possible. Together, they sustain our steadfast mission: providing high-quality, compassionate care to men with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

healthData.name: Health & Well Being
healthData.tagline: Personalized Care for a Full Life

sections.title: Supporting Health, Independence, and Everyday Life

blocks.text: At Good Shepherd Manor, health and wellness support each man’s ability to enjoy the life he chooses. Spending time with friends, exploring interests, participating in Community Day programs, and feeling comfortable at home all depend on care that responds to individual needs.
Our comprehensive health care program supports the men as their needs change, with attention to physical health, emotional well-being, personal choice, and dignity.

sections.title: On-Site Care at the McAllister Infirmary

blocks.text: The 7,000-square-foot McAllister Infirmary provides a welcoming, accessible setting for on-site clinic space that includes medical care, nursing support, wellness services, and rehabilitation. Opened in 2004, the facility includes three examination and treatment rooms, three patient rooms equipped with audio and video monitoring, and rehabilitative equipment.

Nursing professionals are available during normal waking hours. Regular visits from a physician, podiatry services, physical therapy, and access to other specialists help bring care closer to home. Medical supplies and prescription medications further support each man’s individual care needs.

Our nurses get to know each man — his routines, preferences, communication style, and health needs. These relationships help the team recognize changes, respond to concerns, and offer reassurance during difficult moments.

Nursing responsibilities include overseeing medications, monitoring ongoing health conditions, coordinating appointments, and developing individualized care plans with other providers. Preventive care and timely attention to concerns help the men stay comfortable, active, and involved in daily life.
Care also means listening, celebrating progress, and helping each man feel understood and supported.

sections.title: A Voice in Their Own Care

blocks.text: We encourage each man to participate in his health care whenever possible. This may include learning about medications, describing symptoms, asking questions, or making informed choices about daily routines.

Our nursing team advocates for inclusive, respectful care that recognizes each person’s abilities and preferences. Working with families and providers, nurses help reduce barriers to care and support personal choice and self-determination.

Health care at GSM is a shared effort. Nurses collaborate with direct support professionals (DSPs), families, physicians, therapists, pharmacies, and other providers to coordinate services around each man’s needs.

Staff education and training help ensure everyday support is safe, consistent, and aligned with individualized care plans. Communication across departments helps connect medical recommendations with the routines and activities of home life.

When care is needed beyond campus, GSM provides transportation to community medical appointments and transportation back to the Manor following emergency room visits or hospital stays. Coordination with outside providers supports continuity as the men return home.
For men who need hospice services, GSM works with Uplifted Care to support comfort, dignity, and compassionate care in collaboration with each man’s care team and family.

sections.title: Making Home Happen Starts with Health and Wellness

blocks.text: Every health concern addressed, appointment coordinated, and moment of reassurance contributes to life at home. Our nursing team works alongside colleagues throughout GSM to help each man live safely, comfortably, and as independently as possible.
Together, we support the health and well-being that allow the men to enjoy friendships, pursue interests, and thrive in the place they call home.

careersApply.title: Ready to make a difference?
paragraphs: At Good Shepherd Manor, meaningful work begins with everyday connections. Get to know the men, encourage new interests, and celebrate each achievement. Bring your strengths to a team that works together to make each home welcoming and each day count.
Benefits include health, dental, and life insurance, paid time off, a referral program, and a 403(b) plan with matching to help you build your future.

careersBenefits.title: Caring for Our Team
paragraphs: At Good Shepherd Manor, we value the people who make our mission possible. Our benefits are designed to support your health, financial well-being and time away from work, so you can care for yourself and those who matter to you.
Benefits may include health and dental insurance, paid time off and retirement plan options. Eligibility varies by position.
listItems: Paid time off and holiday premium pay

careersCulture.title: A team that cares
paragraphs: At Good Shepherd Manor, caring for others is a team effort. Our staff bring their talents, compassion and dedication together to support the men we serve and create a welcoming community.
From everyday moments to milestones, we support one another and celebrate the difference we make together.

careersIntro.title: Build a career with purpose
paragraphs: At Good Shepherd Manor, your work makes a difference in the lives of the men we serve. Whether providing direct care or supporting our programs and operations, you’ll be part of a team that values dignity, compassion and connection.
Bring your talents, grow your skills and find purpose in work that helps others enjoy meaningful lives. Explore career opportunities at GSM.

endowment.endowmentDisbursement: The Shepherds Endowment Society makes a disbursement annually into the operating budget of Good Shepherd Manor.
endowmentIntro: The Shepherds Endowment Fund was established in 2007 within the Good Shepherd Manor Foundation to provide a continuing source of income for Good Shepherd Manor and to do so in perpetuity.

Endowment gifts are not spent but are invested to generate annual income far beyond the life of the donor. The investment income provides a stable funding source for future operating expenses of Good Shepherd Manor.

endowmentQuote.text: The SES helps the Manor have long-term financial security, which means long-term care for these special men. We want other families to feel the sense of contentment and peace knowing their loved one will have a home providing safe and compassionate care.
endowmentQuote.cite: SES Members – Ed and Joan O’Brien, sister of a former resident
